newsitem.title: USA: Cold remains threat to Mexican coffee - Smith Barney.
newsitem.headline: Cold remains threat to Mexican coffee - Smith Barney.

text.p: An Artic cold front bearing down on central Mexico continued to pose a threat to the northern portion of the country's coffee belt, Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said Wednesday.

With temperatures expected to drop to near freezing Thursday and Friday morning in the far northern reaches of the belt, some frost damage could occur, Davis said in a daily weather update. But the main growing regions should escape serious harm.
"This does not look like a widespread damage event but the potential is there for some damage in some sections of the coffee belt," he said.
"The primary threat right now looks like it will be to coffee in the northern portion of the belt."
Temperatures in the southern coffee zones should fall to around 40 degrees Fahrenheit on Thursday and Friday, with more moderate weather seen for the weekend and early next week, Davis said.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
